_note: Shared worked-example inputs for FMS engineering item 5 (control architecture): guide docs/FMS system design/65_control_architecture.md, tools/fmse/*.py, web/fmse5x*.js. All values are EXAMPLES. Everything here is deterministic: guide, tools and web must give IDENTICAL results (including the cell-controller message log line by line).

_formulas.packml: state machine of ISA-TR88.00.02 exactly as in web/fmse5_data.js (STATES numbers, CMDS numbers, EDGES incl. SC; Stop allowed from every state except Stopped/Stopping/Aborting/Aborted/Clearing; Abort from every state except Aborting/Aborted); commands allowed per mode = web/fmse5_data.js MODES; a command not allowed in the current state or mode is REJECTED (state unchanged, log 'rejected'); 'SC' completes an acting state (rejected in a wait state); mode change only in Stopped, Idle, Aborted
_formulas.tag: tag = site.area.cell.unit.equipment.signal joined by '.', exactly 6 parts; parts 1-5 only A-Z a-z 0-9; the last part (signal) only A-Z a-z 0-9 plus at most one '_' followed by a unit suffix (e.g. SpindleLoad_pct, Torque_Nm, LastCycle_s); unit = unit code + 2-digit number; total length <= max_len (48); signal must not start with a negative word (Not, No, Non, Un) followed by an upper-case letter or the end; duplicates are errors
_formulas.datablock_tags: for every unit instance: the 15 standard data-block items of guide 66 section 8 (web/fmse6_data.js BLOCK names, e.g. Status.StateCurrent = group.item) -> 6-part tag site.area.cell.unit.group.item (the group is the 'equipment' part); plus the module part from web/fmse6_data.js EXTRA for that module code (names like NC.ProgramNo -> group NC); all must pass the tag rule
_formulas.availability: A = MTBF/(MTBF+MTTR) ; series A = product ; parallel (redundant, independent) A = 1 - product(1-A_i) ; downtime h/year = (1-A)*hours_year
_formulas.mes_buffer: MES outages: rate f per year = hours_year/(MTBF+MTTR) of the MES server, exponential outage duration with mean MTTR; a local job buffer of b hours keeps production running; P(outage > b) = exp(-b/MTTR); expected production loss h/year = f*MTTR*exp(-b/MTTR)
_formulas.alarm_kpi: ISA-18.2 / EEMUA 191: alarm count per 10-min window (windows [0,600), [600,1200) ... over the shift); average alarms per hour per operator; peak 10-min count; flood window = more than 10 alarms in the window, % of windows in flood; priority distribution vs target low 80 % / medium 15 % / high 5 % (priority 3 = low, 2 = medium, 1 = high); chattering tag = same tag with >= 3 activations within any 60 s; top-5 bad actors by count (ties: first appearance); targets: <= 6 alarms/h average (~1 per 10 min) acceptable, <= 12 manageable

_rules: Time steps t = 0,1,2,...,T (minutes). In each step do 1-4 in this order.

1 EXTERNAL: apply events with time t (sorted by time, then list order). FAULT: mark the machine faulted (it cannot be routed to); if it is executing, store remaining = end - t, clear end, state Held; otherwise keep its state (Idle or Complete). REPAIRED: clear the fault mark; if remaining stored, end = t + remaining, state Execute; otherwise keep the state. Log 'FAULT m <state>' / 'REPAIRED m <state>'. MES_DOWN / MES_UP switch the MES link (log MES_DOWN / MES_UP).

2 COMPLETIONS with end == t, in this order: vehicle move, then machines by index, then load station. Vehicle move to a machine -> machine starts: state Execute, end = t + machining time of the job of the pallet, log START. Vehicle move to the load station -> pallet appended to the load-station queue (it will be unloaded + reloaded there), a confirmation CONF(job) is put in the outbox, log ARRIVE_LS. Machine end -> state Complete (pallet waits at the machine), log DONE, create vehicle request (pallet, to LS). Load station end -> pallet READY (holds its job), log LOADED.

3 MES: if the MES link is up: send every confirmation in the outbox in order (log SEND_CONF), then if job buffer < job_buffer_max and jobs remain at MES: receive the next job into the buffer (log JOB) - at most ONE job per step. If down: nothing (confirmations stay in the outbox).

4 DECISIONS in this order: (a) load station: if free and its queue is not empty and the job buffer is not empty -> take the first pallet of the queue and the first job of the buffer, end = t + load_min, log LOAD. If the queue is not empty, the buffer is empty AND the MES still has jobs left, count one starved minute (waiting for a job because of the MES link / buffer). (b) READY pallets (in READY order): if a machine is Idle (not reserved, not faulted), reserve the lowest-index such machine for the pallet and create a vehicle request (pallet, to that machine), log ROUTE. (c) vehicle: if free and requests exist, take the first request (FIFO by creation), end = t + move_min, log MOVE.

A machine becomes Idle (and unreserved) again when the vehicle MOVE takes its pallet away (at the start of that move). Initial state: all pallets in the load-station queue in the listed order, machines Idle, vehicle free, job buffer empty, MES up, outbox empty.

Log line format: 't EVENT object details' with t as integer minutes. KPIs at T: jobs started (START), jobs completed (DONE), confirmations sent, outbox at T, max outbox, starved minutes of the load station, machine Execute minutes per machine (minutes t in [start, end) while Execute), MC02 held minutes.
